tools.name: search_reviews
tools.title: Search privacy reviews
tools.description: Search Common Sense Privacy reviews by product name or partial name (case-insensitive, e.g. "facebook" or "zoom"). Use this FIRST whenever the user names a product instead of giving a slug. Returns a `status` of "no_match", "single_match", or "multiple_matches", a list of candidate `matches` (name, slug, score, tier), and a `guidance` string. Follow the guidance: on a single match, call get_review with the returned slug; on multiple matches, show the user the options by name and ask which they mean before calling get_review — never guess; on no match, tell the user no review was found.

query.description: Product name or partial name to search for, e.g. "facebook". Matched as a case-insensitive substring of the product name.

limit.description: Maximum number of candidate matches to return (default 10).

totalMatches.description: Total products matching the query, ignoring the limit.

slug.description: Product slug — the identifier to pass to get_review.

tier.description: Overall privacy rating: Fail, Warning, Pass, or "Common Sense Privacy Seal" for seal holders (the seal supersedes the tier).

evaluatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the evaluation, or null if unknown.

url.description: Canonical public URL of the review.

guidance.description: Instruction for how the model should use this result.

tools.name: get_review
tools.title: Get privacy review
tools.description: Fetch the Common Sense Privacy review for a product by its exact slug (the URL identifier, e.g. "zoom" or "google-classroom"). Returns the product name and logo URL, privacy score, tier, overview, key rating findings, and a link to the full review. If you only have a product name rather than a slug, call search_reviews first to resolve it — do not guess the slug. Present the returned fields (score, tier, evaluation date, and each rating finding) as-is, but omit any field that is null: a null score means a quick rating with no overall score, and a null logoUrl means the product has no logo. The tier already reflects seal status ("Common Sense Privacy Seal" for seal holders), so do not report a separate seal field. Do not add your own interpretation of what the score or tier "means" — report the findings, not editorial commentary.

slug.description: The product slug — the identifier used in the review URL, e.g. "zoom" for privacy.commonsense.org/evaluation/zoom.
Product slug — the identifier to pass to get_review.

logoUrl.description: Absolute URL of the product logo, or null when the product has no logo (omit the logo in that case — do not substitute one).

score.description: Privacy score 0–100 (higher is better), or null for quick ratings, which do not produce an overall score. When null, omit the score and report only the tier.

tier.description: Overall privacy rating to present. One of Fail, Warning, Pass, or "Common Sense Privacy Seal" for seal holders (the seal supersedes the tier). There is no separate seal field.

overview.description: Plain-language summary of the review. Falls back to an auto-generated policy overview when no curated overview exists, so it is always present.

ratingDetails.description: The six key rating findings; empty if no answers exist.

evaluatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the evaluation, or null if unknown.

url.description: Canonical public URL of the review.
